programme: TP73 (a p53-family transcription factor) directly transactivates a growth-arrest/apoptosis checkpoint node — CDKN1A, CDKN2A, CDKN2B, MDM2, TP53, GADD45A, BAX, MLH1 — and three other listed factors converge on the same node from different angles: E4F1 (a p53-cooperating ubiquitin ligase acting at the G1/S transition via CCND1, CCNA2, RASSF1), HOXA5 (a documented inducer of TP53 that also reaches MLH1) and POU6F2 (targeting the CDKN2A/NF1 tumour-suppressor pair). Together these four form a p53/p73-centred cell-cycle-arrest and apoptosis checkpoint module, not four unrelated factors.
role_in_a: In Huntington's disease, p53-family-driven transactivation of arrest and apoptotic genes is one proposed route from mutant-huntingtin stress to neuronal dysfunction and death — cells engage checkpoints they cannot resolve and trip apoptotic effectors.
role_in_b: In psoriatic epidermis the same checkpoint node would be pathogenic in the opposite direction: keratinocytes evading the CDKN1A/CDKN2A-imposed arrest, sustaining the hyperproliferation and apoptosis-resistance that build the plaque.
shared_axis: Both diseases could reflect opposite-direction failure of one p53/p73-centred checkpoint — overactivation driving neuronal loss in HD, underactivation/evasion permitting keratinocyte hyperproliferation in psoriasis — so the same module recurring independently across HD and psoriasis patient groups would point to convergent perturbation of that checkpoint rather than coincidence.
reasoning: The four factors genuinely converge on a nameable p53-family checkpoint through their target genes, but the record does not document this axis for either disease: only TP73 carries a non-trivial Open Targets HD score, its one retrieved paper is flagged as glioblastoma-focused rather than HD-specific, E4F1 and POU6F2 have no disease association at all, and no factor returns any signal for psoriasis. The account rests on general p53-pathway biology, not on anything retrieved for this pair.
support: PMID 30867410 (retrieved for TP73) is about glioblastoma, with no confirmed HD relevance from the text available — does not support the claim. PMID 20565948 (retrieved for HOXA5) is about coronary artery disease gene expression, not HD — does not support the claim. No PMID in the record documents TP73, E4F1, HOXA5, or POU6F2 in Huntington's disease or psoriasis specifically.
how_to_falsify: Profile TP73 and E4F1 chromatin occupancy (ChIP/CUT&RUN) and CDKN1A/CDKN2A/MDM2/GADD45A/BAX expression side by side in HD striatal neurons or HD blood versus lesional psoriatic keratinocytes: the account predicts checkpoint activation (occupancy plus target induction) in HD tissue and checkpoint evasion (occupancy loss or target repression) in psoriatic tissue. Finding no differential occupancy, or the same direction of change in both tissues, would falsify the shared-checkpoint account.
caveats: Only TP73 among the four carrying factors has a meaningful Open Targets HD score (0.87 percentile); HOXA5 is weak (0.39) and E4F1/POU6F2 have none; none of the four has any Open Targets or literature signal for psoriasis in this record. The 168 patient-group comparisons come from only 4 independent cohort pairs, so concordance counts are not fully independent replicates. Twelve tissue-generic immune/hematopoietic factors (FOXO4, PRDM1, NR3C2, EBF1, FOXO3, NFKB2, SPI1, TAL1, RUNX1, GFI1, STAT5B, RELB) were removed before ranking — their absence is by design, not evidence against an immune-mediated account. SOX10 and GATA4 are the only factors in this list with disease-specific record support (both HD-only, via glial/oligodendrocyte and Sertoli-cell/cardiac pathology respectively), but neither fits the p53/p73-checkpoint mechanism named here, so they are present in the pair without being treated as carrying this programme.
